cards.existing: -iyor = -ing (continuous). geliyorum (I'm coming), çalışıyor (he's working). Person ending after: -um (I), -sun (you), -uz (we).

cards.english: Nobody is listening to me.
cards.existing: Negation slides inside the verb as `-me/-ma`. `geliyorum` (I come) → `gelmiyorum` (I don't come). The negation sits between stem and the rest of the suffixes.

cards.english: Let's go, we're running late.

cards.existing: Add -de / -da to a word to say in / at / on. evde (at home), okulda (at school), İstanbul'da (in Istanbul). -de after front vowels, -da after back.

cards.english: Farewell, I will miss you very much.
cards.existing: Future = stem + -ecek/-acak + person. geleceğim (I will come), çalışacaksın (you will work). -ecek after front vowels, -acak after back.

cards.english: You read a newspaper at the office.
cards.existing: -iyor covers both "I am doing now" and "I do generally". Turkish doesn't split habit from continuous the way English does.

cards.existing: Person endings: -im (my), -in (your), -i (his/her), -imiz (our), -iniz (your pl), -leri (their). Vowel harmony picks the right shape: -ım/-um/-üm after back/rounded roots.

cards.existing: Add -de / -da to a word to say in / at / on. evde (at home), okulda (at school), İstanbul'da (in Istanbul). -de after front vowels, -da after back.

cards.existing: Turkish goes Subject-Object-Verb: the verb is the final word. `Ben kitap okuyorum` = 'I book am-reading' = 'I'm reading a book'. The verb wraps everything up.

cards.english: I don't know this city at all.
I don't want coffee, please bring water.
cards.existing: Decoding a long verb? Find -iyor first as your anchor. Read backwards to the root, then forwards to the person ending. Layered like an onion.

cards.existing: -iyor changes shape to match the root: gel-iyor, gör-üyor, kal-ıyor, bul-uyor. The suffix vowel echoes the root vowel.

cards.existing: var = there is/are, yok = there isn't. No "to be" needed. Sınıfta üç kişi var = there are three people in the class.

cards.english: The museum was closed when we arrived.
cards.existing: Yes/no questions use a separate particle: `mi / mı / mu / mü` (vowel harmony). It floats after the questioned word: `Geliyor musun?` (Are you coming?).

cards.english: We work for our children's future.

cards.existing: Turkish vowel harmony: suffixes shape-shift to match the root's last vowel. Two-way harmony picks `-ler/-lar` (plural): front vowels (e, i, ö, ü) → -ler, back vowels (a, ı, o, u) → -lar.

cards.english: I can't speak Turkish but I understand.

cards.existing: Possession 'X of Y' takes two suffixes: -in (genitive) on the owner, -i (possessive) on the thing. `Ali'nin kitabı` = 'Ali's book' literally 'of-Ali book-his'.

cards.english: We watched the football match at the café.
cards.existing: Past tense = stem + di + person. geldim (I came), gördün (you saw), yedi (he ate). The di matches the stem vowel (di / dı / du / dü).

cards.english: My older brother reads books in the evenings.
cards.existing: Possession is baked into the noun: `evim` (my house), `evin` (your house), `evi` (his/her house). No separate 'my', 'your', etc. – just suffix the owner onto the thing.

cards.english: I want to visit the museums in Turkey.
I swear I don't know; I need to ask.

cards.existing: Mentally reorder English sentences as you compose: subject → all objects → all modifiers → verb at the very end. Adjectives stay before their nouns; the verb goes last.

cards.english: The electrician fixed the broken lamp.
I sweep the floor before mopping.
My grandmother told us beautiful stories.
cards.existing: Four-way harmony for `i`-class suffixes: -im/-ım/-um/-üm depending on the last vowel. `Evim` (my house, e→i), `kapım` (my door, a→ı), `kolum` (my arm, o→u), `gözüm` (my eye, ö→ü).

cards.english: Can you speak more slowly, please?
cards.existing: `-(y)abilir/-(y)ebilir` = 'can / may': `gelebilirim` (I can come), `görebilirsin` (you can see). Stacks onto the root: root + a-/-e + bilir + person.

cards.existing: Hardening: after voiceless consonants, the suffix becomes `-ten/-tan`. `Kitaptan` (from the book – kitap ends in p), `evdan`? no, `evden`.

cards.existing: `-ken` = 'while X-ing': `çocukken` (while a child), `yürürken` (while walking). Attaches to nouns, adjectives, or verb-progressive forms.

cards.english: We work very hard for our children's future.

cards.existing: Both ends must match: if owner is in genitive, the thing must carry the possessive suffix. Drop either one and the sentence collapses.

cards.english: I tidy up my desk before starting work.
cards.existing: -den/-dan also marks cause and comparison. soğuktan üşüdüm (cold because of the cold). senden büyük (bigger than you).

cards.existing: If you put the verb in the middle, native speakers will understand but it'll sound foreign or emphatic. Default to verb-last for normal speech.
